title: REPORTED SPEECH
notes:
✓ Reported speech → reporting what someone said without using their exact words.

◆ Direct → She said, "I am tired."
◆ Reported → She said that she was tired.

✓ Direct speech uses quotation marks and the speaker's exact words.
✓ Reported speech changes the sentence to fit the reporting context.

title: BASIC CHANGES
notes:
✓ When the reporting verb is in the past, several changes usually occur:

◆ Tense → may change backward.
◆ Pronouns → change according to the speaker and listener.
◆ Time/place expressions → may change.
◆ Questions → change to statement word order.
◆ Commands/requests → use appropriate infinitive structures.

◆ Direct → He said, "I am busy."
◆ Reported → He said that he was busy.

title: TENSE BACKSHIFT
notes:
◆ Present simple → past simple.
◆ "I work hard." → He said that he worked hard.

◆ Present continuous → past continuous.
◆ "I am working." → He said that he was working.

◆ Present perfect → past perfect.
◆ "I have finished." → She said that she had finished.

◆ Past simple → past perfect.
◆ "I saw him." → She said that she had seen him.

◆ Past continuous → past perfect continuous.
◆ "I was studying." → He said that he had been studying.

◆ Will → would.
◆ "I will help you." → He said that he would help me.

◆ Can → could.
◆ "I can swim." → She said that she could swim.

◆ May → might.
◆ "I may come." → He said that he might come.

title: TENSE CHANGE TABLE
notes:
◆ Present simple → Past simple
◆ Present continuous → Past continuous
◆ Present perfect → Past perfect
◆ Present perfect continuous → Past perfect continuous
◆ Past simple → Past perfect
◆ Past continuous → Past perfect continuous
◆ Will → Would
◆ Can → Could
◆ May → Might

⚠ Past perfect and some modal forms normally do not need further backshift.

◆ "I had finished." → He said that he had finished.
◆ "I could swim." → She said that she could swim.

title: WHEN TENSE DOES NOT CHANGE
notes:
✓ Backshift is not always necessary, especially when the statement is still true or is a general fact.

◆ Direct → The teacher said, "Water boils at 100°C."
◆ Reported → The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.

◆ Direct → He said, "I live in Addis Ababa."
◆ Reported → He said that he lives in Addis Ababa. → if it is still true.

✓ Scientific facts, general truths, and continuing situations can remain in the original tense.

title: PRONOUN CHANGES
notes:
✓ Pronouns change according to who is speaking and who is being addressed.

◆ "I am tired," Sara said.
→ Sara said that she was tired.

◆ "I will help you," John told me.
→ John told me that he would help me.

◆ "We saw them," they said.
→ They said that they had seen them.

✓ Always identify:
◆ 1. Who said it?
◆ 2. Who was being spoken to?
◆ 3. Who/what does each pronoun refer to?

title: TIME & PLACE CHANGES
notes:
✓ Common changes when reporting from a different time/place:

◆ now → then
◆ today → that day
◆ yesterday → the day before / the previous day
◆ tomorrow → the next day / the following day
◆ last week → the previous week
◆ next week → the following week
◆ ago → before
◆ here → there
◆ this → that
◆ these → those

◆ "I will come tomorrow."
→ He said that he would come the next day.

⚠ These changes depend on context; they are not automatic in every situation.

title: SAID VS TOLD
notes:
✓ SAY → usually does not take a person directly after it.
◆ He said that he was tired.
◆ He said to me that he was tired. → possible but less common.

✓ TELL → normally requires an object/person.
◆ He told me that he was tired.

❌ He told that he was tired.
✓ He said that he was tired.

❌ He said me that he was tired.
✓ He told me that he was tired.

✓ Pattern → say + (that) clause.
✓ Pattern → tell + person + (that) clause.

title: REPORTED YES/NO QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Use if or whether for questions that can be answered yes/no.

◆ Direct → "Are you ready?"
◆ Reported → He asked me if I was ready.

◆ Direct → "Did she come?"
◆ Reported → He asked whether she had come.

⚠ Reported questions use statement word order.

❌ He asked me if was I ready.
✓ He asked me if I was ready.

❌ She asked where did he go.
✓ She asked where he had gone.

title: REPORTED WH-QUESTIONS
notes:
✓ Keep the question word: who, what, where, when, why, how, etc.

◆ "Where do you live?"
→ She asked me where I lived.

◆ "Why did he leave?"
→ She asked why he had left.

◆ "What are you doing?"
→ He asked what I was doing.

⚠ Do not use question word order or do/does/did in the reported clause.

❌ She asked where did I live.
✓ She asked where I lived.

title: REPORTED COMMANDS & ORDERS
notes:
✓ Use → reporting verb + object + to + V1.

◆ "Open the door," he said to me.
→ He told me to open the door.

◆ "Work hard," the teacher said.
→ The teacher told us to work hard.

✓ Negative command → not to + V1.

◆ "Don't touch it."
→ He told me not to touch it.

✓ Common reporting verbs → tell, order, instruct, command, warn.

title: REQUESTS & ADVICE
notes:
✓ Requests → ask + object + to + V1.

◆ "Please help me."
→ She asked me to help her.

✓ Advice → advise + object + to + V1.

◆ "You should study harder."
→ The teacher advised me to study harder.

✓ Warning → warn + object + not to + V1.

◆ "Don't go there."
→ He warned me not to go there.

✓ Choose the reporting verb according to the speaker's intention.

title: REPORTED SUGGESTIONS
notes:
✓ Suggestions can be reported using several structures.

◆ "Let's go home."
→ He suggested going home.

◆ "Let's study together."
→ She suggested that we study together.

✓ Suggest + V-ing.
✓ Suggest + that + subject + base verb is also possible.

❌ He suggested me to go home.
✓ He suggested going home.
✓ He suggested that I go home.

⚠ Suggest normally does not take object + to-infinitive.

title: REPORTED OFFERS & PROMISES
notes:
✓ Offer → offer + to + V1.

◆ "I'll carry your bag."
→ He offered to carry my bag.

✓ Promise → promise + to + V1.

◆ "I will help you."
→ She promised to help me.

✓ Refusal → refuse + to + V1.

◆ "I won't do it."
→ He refused to do it.

✓ The reporting verb should express the original intention.

title: REQUEST, ORDER OR QUESTION?
notes:
◆ "Close the door."
→ He told me to close the door. → order.

◆ "Could you close the door?"
→ He asked me to close the door. → request.

◆ "Did you close the door?"
→ He asked me if I had closed the door. → question.

✓ Identify the function before choosing the reporting structure.

title: REPORTING VERBS
notes:
✓ Common reporting verbs:

◆ say → said that...
◆ tell → told + object + that...
◆ ask → asked if/whether or wh-word...
◆ order → ordered + object + to...
◆ advise → advised + object + to...
◆ warn → warned + object + not to...
◆ remind → reminded + object + to...
◆ invite → invited + object + to...
◆ offer → offered to...
◆ promise → promised to...
◆ refuse → refused to...
◆ agree → agreed to...
◆ suggest → suggested + V-ing / that-clause
◆ admit → admitted + V-ing / that-clause
◆ explain → explained that...

✓ Choose the reporting verb based on meaning, not only grammar.

title: MODAL CHANGES
notes:
✓ Some modal verbs commonly change in reported speech:

◆ will → would
◆ can → could
◆ may → might
◆ shall → would/should, depending on meaning

◆ "I will help you."
→ He said that he would help me.

◆ "I can drive."
→ She said that she could drive.

◆ "I may come."
→ He said that he might come.

⚠ Must can remain must when expressing a continuing necessity or logical conclusion, but may change to had to when it refers to past obligation.

◆ "I must leave now."
→ He said that he had to leave then. → past obligation.

◆ "You must be careful."
→ He said that I must be careful. → continuing advice/necessity.

title: DIRECT → REPORTED FORMULAS
notes:
◆ Statement → said/told + (that) + clause.

◆ Yes/No question → asked + if/whether + clause.

◆ WH-question → asked + wh-word + clause.

◆ Command → told + object + to + V1.

◆ Negative command → told + object + not to + V1.

◆ Request → asked + object + to + V1.

◆ Advice → advised + object + to + V1.

◆ Suggestion → suggested + V-ing / that-clause.

◆ Offer → offered + to + V1.

◆ Promise → promised + to + V1.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ He said me that he was tired.
✓ He told me that he was tired.

❌ She asked me where did I live.
✓ She asked me where I lived.

❌ He told me don't go.
✓ He told me not to go.

❌ She suggested me to study.
✓ She suggested studying.

❌ He asked that was I ready.
✓ He asked if I was ready.

❌ She said that "she was tired."
✓ She said that she was tired.

❌ He told to me that he was busy.
✓ He told me that he was busy.

✓ Main rule → Reported speech is normally written as a statement, not as the original question or command.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Identify whether the sentence is a statement, question, command, request, suggestion, offer, or promise.

◆ 2. Choose the correct reporting verb.

◆ 3. Change pronouns according to the context.

◆ 4. Check whether tense backshift is required.

◆ 5. Change time/place expressions when the context requires it.

◆ 6. For questions, use statement word order.

◆ 7. For commands/requests, use object + to + V1.

◆ 8. For negative commands, use object + not to + V1.

◆ 9. Check say vs tell.

◆ 10. Check that quotation marks are removed in reported speech.

✓ QUICK MEMORY:
◆ Statement → said/told + that
◆ Yes/No question → asked + if/whether
◆ WH-question → asked + WH-word
◆ Command → told + object + to
◆ Negative command → told + object + not to
◆ Request → asked + object + to
◆ Suggestion → suggested + V-ing / that-clause
◆ Offer → offered + to
◆ Promise → promised + to

✓ Golden rule → Reported speech changes the form of the original sentence while keeping its meaning.
